site_article.answer_summary: Yes, some ChatGPT Plus users can now get dots: OpenAI started a limited test on November 19, 2026. Dots were first offered to Pro, Business Premium and Enterprise users, and are now also coming to all Business Standard users.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI has started testing ChatGPT dots, its always on assistant, with a small number of ChatGPT Plus subscribers, 9to5Mac reported on November 19, 2026. Thibault Sottiaux, who leads engineering for Codex and ChatGPT, announced the test and said dots are also coming to all ChatGPT Business Standard users.

OpenAI announced dots in September and first offered them to Pro, Business Premium and Enterprise subscribers, according to 9to5Mac. The company described them as running on GPT-6 Astra, with their own cloud computer, the ability to learn from feedback over time and to work toward a user's goals around the clock, and connections to more than 4,000 apps through plugins.
What changes for Plus and Business users

9to5Mac called the Plus test limited and said it is not yet clear whether Plus and Business Standard subscribers will get the same usage allowances as the higher tiers. For Pro and Business Premium users, conversations with a dot do not count toward regular usage limits, although more complex tasks have separate allowances, and work handed to ChatGPT Work or Codex counts toward those products' limits.

Digital Trends reported that OpenAI's help pages describe the Business Standard expansion as reaching eligible members in the United States. Recent additions to dots, according to 9to5Mac, include iOS widgets, Shortcuts support, replies straight from iOS notifications, custom instructions, and a beta that lets US Pro subscribers message their dot through iMessage, or RCS on Android.
A new layout for the ChatGPT mobile app

Sottiaux also shared a demo of a redesigned ChatGPT mobile app on November 19, Digital Trends reported. It starts with Pro users who already have a dot or are eligible to create one, and a small group of eligible Plus users will see it too. Some users get the layout by default, while others can switch it on or off with a New ChatGPT Design option in Settings.

The new design uses a bottom tab bar with a Home tab, a dedicated Dot tab and a grid of other tools, including Projects, Images, Scheduled, Codex, Plugins, Finance, Health and Sites. Pressing and holding an item pins it to the tab bar. According to Digital Trends, the rollout is for users 18 or older where dots are available, and it excludes the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and South Korea.

Moving dots down to the Plus plan and giving them a permanent place in the app suggests OpenAI wants the always on assistant to become a standard part of ChatGPT rather than a premium extra. How generous the Plus allowances turn out to be will decide whether that happens.
Watch whether OpenAI widens the Plus test to all subscribers and publishes usage limits for Plus and Business Standard, which would show how much ongoing work a dot can do on a cheaper plan.
